newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ to announce Feb long-term prime rate Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: IBJ to announce Feb long-term prime rate Wednesday.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Friday it will announce its long-term prime rate for February and the coupon rate on its February five-year bank debentures next Wednesday.
The February long-term prime rate is likely to be left unchanged at a record low 2.5 percent, bank sources said.
The long-term prime rate, applied to loans of one year and longer to the bank's most creditworthy clients, was last cut in December to 2.5 percent from 2.7 percent in November.
IBJ, the largest of Japan's three long-term credit banks, left the coupon rate on its January five-year debentures unchanged at a record low 1.6 percent.
IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above the coupon of its benchmark five-year debenture. The bank revises the rates every month to reflect market trends.

A final decision is likely to be made after it sees the debenture yields in the secondary market early next week, the sources said. IBJ's 1.6 percent December debenture was traded at a yield of 1.62 percent on Friday morning, bond traders said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
